This deletes the app’s password on your server and removes the library and cached photos from this phone. The picker’s Nextcloud tab stays empty until you sign in again.

Enter your server’s address. You approve access on your server’s own sign-in page, and this app gets its own app password, which you can revoke in Nextcloud under Settings, Security.

Changing folders rebuilds the library. The picker’s Nextcloud tab empties and fills again as the new folders are listed.
Apps with their own photo grid

Some apps, such as Messenger, show their own photo grid instead of Android’s picker, so your Nextcloud photos can’t appear there. Use Send from Nextcloud instead: long-press this app’s icon, or add its Quick Settings tile. Pick your photos, then choose the app to send them to.

Only one cloud source can be active at a time. With Google Photos kept as a choice, you switch between it and this app in the photo picker’s cloud settings. On some phones, such as GrapheneOS, that settings screen only appears after a restart. Updating this app deselects it; with Shizuku it is selected again automatically, otherwise a notification takes you to the settings.
